title: Blood Type Punnett Square Calculator + Self-Test
description: Pick two parent blood types and see every child type with the odds, then test yourself on six questions with the square behind each answer.
intro: Six questions on ABO genotypes, which parent pairs can and cannot make which child, and Rh as a separate gene, each answer checkable against the squares above.

questions.q: Both parents are type A. Can they have a type O child?
options: No, an O child needs at least one type O parent
No, a type A parent cannot carry the O allele
Yes, two AO parents give OO one in four times
Only if one parent is secretly type AB
questions.why: Type A blood is either AA or AO, so two AO parents can each pass the O allele they were carrying silently.
questions.source: FAQ, 'Can two parents with type A blood have a type O child?': 'If both parents are AO, each can pass the O allele, so there is a 1 in 4 chance of an OO child, who is type O.' Square AO x AO fills with AA, AO, AO, OO, so 1 of the 4 boxes is OO. The page's own assertion checks it: t("AO","AO").A===3 && t("AO","AO").O===1.

questions.q: An AB parent and an O parent, standard alleles only. Which child types are possible?
options: Type A or type B, never AB and never O
Type AB or type O, with nothing in between
All four types, each one in four odds
Only type AB, since AB is codominant
questions.why: An AB parent passes either A or B while an OO parent can only pass O, so every child comes out AO or BO.
questions.source: Flag box, 'The one cross worth memorising': 'AB passes A or B, O passes O, so every child is AO or BO.' Square AB x OO fills with AO, AO, BO, BO, which is 2/4 type A and 2/4 type B, and the page asserts it: !t("AB","OO").AB && !t("AB","OO").O.

questions.q: Which parent pairing can produce all four blood types?
options: An AB parent with another AB parent
A type O parent with another type O parent
An AB parent with a type O parent
A type A parent with a type B parent
questions.why: Only AO crossed with BO puts an A, a B and two O alleles into the same square, so AB, A, B and O are all reachable.
questions.source: FAQ, 'What blood types can a type A and a type B parent have?': 'All four. If both parents are heterozygous (AO and BO), the children can be AB, A, B or O, each with a 1 in 4 chance. It is the only phenotype pairing that can produce every blood type.' Square AO x BO fills with AB, AO, BO, OO, one box each, and the page asserts Object.keys(t("AO","BO")).length===4.

questions.q: A blood test gives the type. For which types does that also fix the genotype?
options: Type A and type B, because both of those are dominant
Type AB and type O, the two unambiguous ones
Every type, a blood test reads the genotype
No type at all, genotypes need family trees
questions.why: A and B both mask O, so type A could be AA or AO, while AB and O each have only one genotype that fits them.
questions.source: Section 'Why a blood type is not a genotype': 'Only AB and O are unambiguous: AB must be AB, and O must be OO.' The page's GENO table says the same thing in data: A:["AA","AO"], B:["BB","BO"], AB:["AB"], O:["OO"], so A and B have two genotypes each and AB and O have exactly one.

questions.q: Both parents are Rh positive and both carry a hidden d. Odds of an Rh negative child?
options: 1 in 4, the one dd box of the four
Zero, Rh positive parents stay positive
1 in 2, since d is carried by both of them
3 in 4, matching the dominant ratio here
questions.why: Rh positive can be DD or Dd, and only a Dd by Dd cross leaves a dd box, which is one box out of four.
questions.source: Section 'Rh factor is a separate gene': 'Two Rh positive parents who both carry a hidden d have a 1 in 4 chance of an Rh negative child.' Dd x Dd fills with DD, Dd, Dd, dd, so dd is 1 of 4. The page's rhOdds assertion says rhOdds("+","+").lo===0.75, so the Rh positive chance bottoms out at 75% and the negative chance tops out at 25%.

questions.q: Why is ABO called codominance rather than incomplete dominance?
options: Because O is recessive to both A and B alleles
Because three alleles exist instead of just two
Because AB blood sits midway between A and B
Because AB cells show both antigens, no blend
questions.why: Codominance means both gene products appear in full, while incomplete dominance would give one intermediate phenotype instead.
questions.source: FAQ, 'Why is ABO inheritance called codominance?': 'when someone inherits both A and B, neither masks the other and both antigens appear on the red blood cells, giving type AB. That is different from incomplete dominance, where you would get a blend.' The page's pheno() function returns "AB" whenever a genotype includes both A and B, with no intermediate category, and the three-allele point is filed separately under multiple allelism.
